selection_detail: Standalone Tier-1d demand-driven refill run (buffer starved: claimable=6 < floor=36; all mobile-native/KMP-gated vectors are structurally unlandable in the cloud runner, so a NON-mobile-native segment was required). REVIEW_CURSOR in state.json is stale relative to the actual signals/*.json coverage, so selection used real signal-file coverage as the source of truth. By run time (2026-08-29) today's Tier-1d runs had already covered api-core (client-ip, workflow-docgen), api-handlers, mobile-rn, ppt-web-core (routes-fetch-i18n), ppt-web-ui, and reality-web. Among the landable non-mobile segments, reality-server (last reviewed 2026-08-28) was the only one NOT yet touched today -> oldest-unreviewed. Saturation check: zero OPEN code-review-finding backlog items for reality-server (only mobile-native-kmp has 3 open, and it is excluded as non-landable), so no saturation-skip. The prior 2026-08-28 reality-server run already captured the two obvious SSO issues (code-review-reality-server-sso-sessions-unbounded = in-memory sso_sessions map in state.rs:855; code-review-reality-server-sso-reqwest-no-timeout = reqwest client w/o timeout in sso.rs:687), so this run deliberately reviewed DIFFERENT files/concerns for net-new distinct findings. Static-only Rust review: grep sweep for unwrap()/expect() (all 32 non-test hits are guarded, test-only, or boot-time config fail-fast: inquiries/mod.rs:266 chars().next().unwrap() is guarded by the len>=9 check at :261; extractors/auth.rs:63 strip_prefix().unwrap() is guarded by the matching find() predicate; state.rs panics are JWT_SECRET boot validation), todo!()/unimplemented!()/unsafe (none in prod paths), StatusCode::OK on error branches (health.rs 200-for-degraded is intentional+commented), dynamic SQL (listings.rs:700 format! interpolates only a static const with $1/$2 binds via AssertSqlSafe; pagination clamp_pagination clamps 1..=100, tested), IDOR/user-scoping (favorites.rs + saved_searches.rs consistently pass principal.user_id; inquiries mark_as_read/respond are realtor_id-scoped per #519), email header/CRLF injection (services/email.rs parses to/from via lettre Mailbox::parse which rejects CRLF; subject is a static const; user name goes only into the plaintext body), secret logging (no token/secret/password VALUES in tracing calls), and public-input bounds (inquiry name<=100, message 10..2000, email<=254 all bounded). The one net-new landable finding below concerns the agency-import feed-URL SSRF boundary.
note: reality-server (Rust) -- agency-import feed-URL SSRF: submit-time validation is static-IP-only by design and defers fetch-time re-resolution to an out-of-segment worker. Landable in the cloud runner (Rust, no mobile-native/AGP dependency): reuse the existing resolving helper backend/crates/common/src/url_validation.rs (lookup_host + is_forbidden_ip) at the reality-portal import fetch boundary and add a reality-server-side defence-in-depth re-check. Deliberately did NOT re-emit the 2026-08-28 SSO findings, nor widen sso-reqwest-no-timeout to the sibling unbounded clients at sso.rs:711/748 (same class/file as the existing finding). Segment is otherwise high quality; only 1 defensible net-new vector found.

evidence: The agency-import feed-URL SSRF defence is only half-wired inside the reality-server segment. routes/agency_imports.rs:238 and :290 call crate::util::url_validator::validate_fetch_url(url) at SUBMIT time only. That validator is static-IP-only by construction: util/url_validator.rs:116 validate_fetch_url rejects literal private/loopback/link-local/cloud-metadata IPs (incl. ::ffff:169.254.169.254 unmapping), but its own module docs at url_validator.rs:13-14 and the fn doc at :113 state 'Hostnames (domains) pass this check; the import worker MUST re-resolve and re-validate the resolved IP at fetch time to defend against DNS-rebinding', and the inline note at :175 repeats 'Hostnames must be re-validated at fetch time by the worker'.

So any feed URL whose HOST is a domain name (not a literal IP) passes the submit-time check unconditionally. Without a fetch-time re-resolution+re-validation step, an attacker registers a hostname that resolves to 169.254.169.254 (AWS/GCP metadata) or an internal 10.x/127.0.0.1 address -- or uses DNS-rebinding to flip the answer between the submit check and the fetch -- and the import worker fetches it, i.e. SSRF to cloud metadata / internal services.

The correct fetch-time guard already EXISTS in the workspace and is used by sibling servers: backend/crates/common/src/url_validation.rs:292 does tokio::net::lookup_host((host, port)) and then is_forbidden_ip(ip) (lines 162-167/233/299); api-server already applies this defence-in-depth pattern at routes/integrations/webhook.rs:527 ('SSRF gate: re-validate the stored URL as defence-in-depth') and services/actions/api_call.rs:142 (lookup_host). The reality-portal agency-import path does not visibly route through that resolving helper anywhere inside the reality-server segment.

Fix (landable, Rust, no mobile dependency): at the reality-portal import fetch boundary (the worker in backend/crates/db/src/repositories/reality_portal/imports.rs and/or a reality-server-side wrapper before the outbound fetch), call common::url_validation's resolving variant (lookup_host + is_forbidden_ip) on the stored feed URL immediately before fetching, and reject on a forbidden resolved IP -- matching the api-server webhook.rs:527 pattern. Add reality-server-side defence-in-depth so the guarantee does not depend solely on the worker crate. IG3: a test that an import whose feed hostname resolves to a private/metadata IP is rejected at fetch time (not just at submit time).

Confidence medium (not high): the actual outbound feed download lives in the db crate (crates/db/repositories/reality_portal/imports.rs), OUTSIDE the reviewed reality-server segment, so this static pass could NOT directly confirm whether that worker already calls common::url_validation's resolving check before fetching. A backend-wide grep for to_socket_addrs/lookup_host/is_forbidden_ip shows the resolving helper exists and is used by api-server, but did not surface a reality-portal-import caller -- hence the finding is scoped as 'verify + add explicit reality-server-side re-validation' (defence-in-depth on an SSRF-class surface) rather than a confirmed live vulnerability. Severity reflects SSRF-to-metadata impact IF the worker lacks the re-check; confidence reflects the unconfirmed out-of-segment fetch path.
